1:56 to 28mm

A precise guide to converting 1:56 scale models into 28mm equivalents for seamless tabletop integration.

Recommended Scale

89.6%
Open in Engine

Mathematical Proof

(28.0mm / 28.6mm) * 100 = 89.6%

Scale Baselines

  • Source (1:56 Bolt Action) 28.6mm Eye
  • Target (28mm True Scale) 28.0mm Eye

About This Calculation

STLACCESS uses the 175cm human baseline with eye-level measurement (160cm) as the standard for fantasy and sci-fi miniatures. This method accounts for variable headgear and base heights that make "total height" scaling unreliable. Read the full methodology →

When You Need This

This is commonly used when fitting oversized 1:56 heroes or monsters into a smaller 28mm regiment, or when printing 1:56 STL files for a 28mm game system. This downscale is noticeable but manageable. Many painters use the size gap to add basing detail, slight posture adjustments, or custom base rims to bridge the visual difference.

Source Scale: 1:56

1:56 is the wargaming vehicle companion scale. Often paired with 28mm infantry. Tanks and vehicles at 1:56 look correct next to 28mm figures because the vehicle scale accounts for ground clearance and hull height, not just eye level. Common systems: Bolt Action, Chain of Command, Flames of War (vehicle scale).

Note: Some manufacturers label 1:48 vehicles as 'compatible with 28mm.' They are slightly oversized. Stick to 1:56 for visual harmony.

Target Scale: 28mm

28mm is used by Dungeons & Dragons, Pathfinder, Oldhammer. The classic tabletop standard. Measures to the eyes (160cm on a 175cm human), not the top of the head. Helmets, top-knots, and ornate headgear often add 2–4mm of perceived height.

Note: Older sculpts may be closer to 25mm true-scale. Always verify the sculptor's baseline before scaling.

Resin & Print Settings

When resin printing 1:56 → 28mm, apply +1.5% shrinkage compensation on top of the 89.6% scale factor. In FDM, fdm printers rarely need compensation; slight over-extrusion usually cancels any shrinkage. 1:56 tanks are the sweet spot for fdm printing: large enough for detail, small enough to print quickly.
